title: The honest scoreboard
learning_goal: See the 'how often' payoff with its error bars, why a smooth generator must lag a steep onset, and what remains weak.
takeaway: On a toy model the crossing rate is predicted from generated snapshots and the model's equations, without running time forward: roughly right far from the threshold and poorly near it, as expected from a generator that varies smoothly with the knob.

badge.note: E1 · model C, seed 0 · 20,000 generated snapshots per Γ

y.label: crossing rate of D (per unit time)

promise_card.verdict: ✓ far from the threshold · ≈ near it

sentences.text: The toll counter is back: every car is now {model}generated{/}.
They come from the machine with the built-in mirror: twenty thousand at each of forty-one settings of {param}Gamma{/}, most unseen in training.
Rice, with the equations, turns them into a {metric}crossing rate{/}.
Against the counted truth, far from the threshold, the {metric}cumulative error{/} is fourteen percent.
Setting by setting, the miss averages seventeen percent, and reaches sixty-five percent at two settings.
Near the threshold, the error climbs to forty-two percent.
One model, one training seed.
Rice needs the equations, and gives a rate, not waiting times.
So, the study's third question: can a machine tell us {metric}how often{/}?
For crossings on three dials: far from the threshold, roughly yes; near it, not yet.

formulas.tex: \hat r_0 = \frac{1}{2h}\cdot\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} |\dot D_i|\,\mathbf{1}_{|D_i| < h},\qquad \dot D_i = -0.1\,D_i + V_i Q_i\ \text{on each generated snapshot};\quad h = 0.2,\ N = 20\,000 \text{ per } \Gam

\text{cumulative error} = \frac{\sum_{\Gam} \big|\hat r_0^{\,\mathrm{Rice}}[\cm{q}] - r_0^{\,\mathrm{count}}\big|}{\sum_{\Gam} r_0^{\,\mathrm{count}}}:\ \ 14\%\ (\Gam \ge 0.89),\ \ 42\%\ (0.865 \le \Gam \le 0.885);\ \ \text{pointwise, far: mean } 17\%,\ \max 65\%

scenes.title: Predict: early, late or on time?

badge.note: E1 · fine grid · model C, seed 0

predict.title: PREDICT
predict.question: Near the threshold, will the generated rate switch on early, late, or on time?

sentences.text: Zoom in. The truth is silent up to zero point eight six.
But the machine changes smoothly with {param}Gamma{/}.
Will its crossing rate switch on early, late, or on time?
Early and late, but never on time.
Below the threshold, it leaks false crossings: up to a tenth of the rate just above.
At zero point eight six five, it is late: less than a sixth of the counted rate.
Just above, it overshoots: five crossings per thousand time units, against three point four.

scenes.title: A stiff sheet on a steep ramp

badge.note: Prop. 9, a lower bound · E1 consistent with it, seed 0

metaphor.ramp_from: sweep.bridge_fine.reference (monotone envelope of the fine-grid bridge mass)

sentences.text: Why? Picture the machine as a stiff sheet: as {param}Gamma{/} turns, its crowd changes only so fast.
The truth climbs a steep ramp: just above zero point eight six, the corridor opens.
The sheet rounds the corner: too early, then too low.
The data show both: early strays in the corridor, then too few at the threshold.
A theorem: at a true jump, a smooth machine misses by at least half of it.
Unless it is very supple, or told which state the system is in.
Here, a ramp, not a jump, and one seed: consistent with the theorem, not proof.
Nor does the theorem explain the overshoot.

labels: unless: very supple, or told which state

sentences.text: The scoreboard: eight mechanisms, each with a verdict.
For every snapshot: hill maps and projection, exact; the penalty, approximate.
For the crowd: the mirror, exact; the crowd loss, useful but not clean; the rest, failures.
Back to the study's three questions.
One: between the dots, the shapes come out right, but no model reaches its {metric}noise floor{/}.
Two: each law where it holds, exactly yes, {metric}on average{/} partly.
Three, {metric}how often{/}: roughly right far from the threshold, poor near it.
Three lessons.
Exact laws: build them in.
Crowd laws: impose them on the crowd, never on each snapshot.
And judge every result against the noise floor, with enough seeds.

question.en: Which settings should get runs long enough to *count* reversals, so a predicted rate can be *checked*?
question.say: Which settings should get runs long enough to count reversals, so a predicted rate can be checked?
question.fr: Pour quels réglages faut-il des simulations assez longues pour *compter* les renversements, afin de *vérifier* un taux prédit ?
question.why: A predicted rate is only checked against a count: E1 counted 93 to 572 crossings per setting. The reversal simulations hold few reversals, and the configured Taylor–Green runs keep 40 time units.
question.unblocks: Run length and trajectories per setting (t_keep, n_traj), which settings get long runs and which only snapshots, and the error bar a rate is judged by (5 % or a Poisson interval).
question.why_fr: Un taux prédit ne se vérifie que contre un comptage : E1 a compté de 93 à 572 passages par réglage. Les simulations de renversements en contiennent peu, et les simulations Taylor–Green configurées ne gardent que 40 unités de temps.
question.unblocks_fr: La durée et le nombre de trajectoires par réglage (t_keep, n_traj), les réglages qui reçoivent de longues simulations et ceux qui ne fournissent que des instantanés, et la barre d'erreur qui juge un taux (5 % ou un intervalle de Poisson).
